title: DN-QSM: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping via Laplacian Field Estimation and Regularized Null-Space Correction

synopsis.Motivation: Background-field contamination and ill-conditioned dipole inversion limit quantitative susceptibility mapping.
synopsis.Goal(s): Develop a reconstruction architecture that separates field estimation, analytic inversion, and learned spectral correction.
synopsis.Approach: DN-QSM couples two 3D U-Nets through a Tikhonov-regularized inverse and regularized null projection. Evaluation used a COSMOS simulation and Graz1 data.
synopsis.Results: On COSMOS, normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) decreased from 44.38% after initialization to 37.36% after correction, a 15.8% relative reduction. Supplied iQSM and pretrained NeXtQSM yielded 48.97% and 76.96%. Graz1 enabled qualitative assessment without reference susceptibility.

impact: DN-QSM integrates analytic dipole inversion with learned correction concentrated at poorly conditioned frequencies. Reduced COSMOS reconstruction error motivates further evaluation of this architecture; Graz1 demonstrates application to additional data, with quantitative generalization remaining to be established.

body.INTRODUCTION: Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) estimates tissue susceptibility from magnetic-field perturbations. Background-field contamination complicates local-field recovery, while zeros of the dipole kernel make susceptibility inversion ill-conditioned.[1] Learned approaches, including NeXtQSM[2] and iQSM,[3] address reconstruction through data-driven mappings. We introduce DN-QSM, an architecture that explicitly separates Laplacian-guided local-field estimation, Tikhonov-regularized inversion, and learned spectral correction. The central design is to weight the correction toward frequencies attenuated by the regularized inverse. We evaluate this formulation using a COSMOS-based simulation and Graz1 data.
body.METHODS:
The architecture comprises two separately parameterized 3D U-Nets (Figure 1). The masked total field is mean-centered and extended outside the brain mask before a Fourier-domain discrete Laplacian is applied. This extension avoids differentiating an abrupt mask truncation. The first network estimates the local field, using root-mean-square (RMS) normalization of the Laplacian input and a normalized-field skip connection. Both networks use residual instance normalization to retain an amplitude-dependent feature pathway.

Let $D$ denote the dipole kernel, $\mathcal{F}$ the Fourier transform, and $\hat b_{\mathrm{loc}}$ the estimated local field. The initial susceptibility is $\chi_0=\mathcal{F}^{-1}[K_\tau\mathcal{F}(\hat b_{\mathrm{loc}})]$, with $K_\tau=D/(D^2+\tau^2)$ and $\tau=0.1$. The second network receives RMS-normalized $\chi_0$ and predicts a residual, rescaled to susceptibility units as $r_\phi$. The final reconstruction is $\hat\chi=\chi_0+\mathcal{F}^{-1}[P_\tau\mathcal{F}(r_\phi)]$, where $P_\tau=\tau^2/(D^2+\tau^2)$. The regularized null projection is a smooth spectral weighting that emphasizes frequencies with small $|D|$.

Training used 105 original susceptibility samples, partitioned into 95 training and 10 validation samples. Simulations included exterior-source background fields, noise, susceptibility lesions, and localized dephasing. Joint supervision combined local-field, field-gradient, exterior-field, initial-susceptibility, final-susceptibility, and dipole-consistency losses. The final joint fine-tuning run comprised 30 epochs from pretrained weights using AdamW, batch size 8, and initial learning rate $3\times10^{-5}$. Epoch 18 was selected by minimum COSMOS normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE).

The quantitative experiment used one fixed COSMOS-based simulation with a $160^3$ reference grid, 1-mm isotropic spacing, simulated background fields, and SNR 100. Comparisons included the Tikhonov initialization, official pretrained NeXtQSM, and a supplied iQSM reconstruction. NRMSE was computed over the full three-dimensional brain mask without fitted intensity scaling, offset correction, or mean removal.

Graz1 contained six echoes (TE 4.92-29.52 ms; approximately $0.80\times0.80\times2.0$-mm voxels). Supplied unwrapped phase underwent magnitude-squared-weighted echo-time fitting, conversion to ppm, and resampling to 1-mm isotropic resolution. DN-QSM used $184^3$ and $201^3$ inference grids for COSMOS and Graz1; NeXtQSM used $192^3$ and $256^3$. Outputs were cropped to common brain regions. Graz1 was evaluated qualitatively because reference susceptibility was unavailable.
body.RESULTS: COSMOS NRMSE was 44.38% for the Tikhonov initialization and 37.36% for final DN-QSM, corresponding to a reduction of 7.02 percentage points (15.8% relative). Supplied iQSM and pretrained NeXtQSM yielded 48.97% and 76.96%, respectively. Figure 2 presents reconstructions and signed reference differences under identical display limits. Graz1 reconstructions (Figure 3) exhibited differences in tissue and vascular contrast across methods. Residual streaking remained visible near strong susceptibility sources; the available data do not support a quantitative accuracy ranking for Graz1.
body.DISCUSSION: The COSMOS experiment supports the proposed combination of analytic initialization and frequency-weighted learned correction. Its explicit additive decomposition identifies the contribution beyond regularized inversion. However, the experiment does not isolate the effects of Laplacian preprocessing, normalization, or spectral weighting. COSMOS also guided checkpoint selection, making the reported error a development result. Only one simulation and one Graz1 dataset were evaluated; independence of the training samples and COSMOS reference remains unverified. Method-specific padding and unavailable iQSM inference settings further limit comparator interpretation. Independent datasets, controlled preprocessing, and component ablations are required to assess generalization and attribute performance gains.
body.CONCLUSION: DN-QSM combines Laplacian-guided field estimation with Tikhonov inversion and regularized null correction. It reduced COSMOS development-case NRMSE by 15.8% relative to initialization and produced Graz1 susceptibility maps, motivating independent quantitative validation.

figures.name: Architecture
figures.caption: DN-QSM architecture. A boundary-aware Laplacian precedes local-field estimation by a 3D U-Net. A Tikhonov-regularized inverse provides initial susceptibility. A second 3D U-Net predicts a residual; regularized null projection weights this residual before addition to the initial estimate. Blue denotes learned modules; gold denotes fixed operators.

figures.name: COSMOS
figures.caption: COSMOS comparison: susceptibility reconstructions (top) and signed reference differences (bottom). Columns: NeXtQSM, iQSM, Tikhonov initialization (Soft-TKD), final DN-QSM, and reference. Titles report whole-mask 3D NRMSE. Grayscale limits are +/-0.1 ppm for susceptibility and +/-0.02 ppm for differences. COSMOS also guided checkpoint selection.

figures.name: Graz1
figures.caption: Qualitative Graz1 comparison. Columns: NeXtQSM, supplied iQSM2 reconstruction, Tikhonov initialization (Soft-TKD), and final DN-QSM. Each column shows matched central axial, sagittal, and coronal views with grayscale limits of +/-0.1 ppm. Reference susceptibility was unavailable; no NRMSE or quantitative accuracy ranking is reported.

Confirm the provenance and independence of the 105 original samples, the COSMOS reference, and Graz1; do not equate samples with independent participants. Confirm whether Graz1 is acquired, modified, or blended data and provide the applicable acquisition and ethics/consent details.
Verify the earlier checkpoint's complete training history. The reported 30 epochs describe only the final fine-tuning stage; this is not training from scratch.

Confirm that the supplied iQSM files were reconstructed from the intended COSMOS and Graz1 inputs, and document iQSM version, settings, and output units. Their input/inference provenance is not available in the current files.

COSMOS was used for checkpoint selection, so the reported NRMSE is a development-case result. Original training/reference overlap has not been established. No claims of independent test-set performance, population significance, or clinical superiority are made.

Method-specific padding is preserved. DN-QSM uses 184-cubed/201-cubed grids, and NeXtQSM uses 192-cubed/256-cubed grids. Padding changes can alter DN-QSM outputs, so future comparisons should report and control this choice.

Figure labels Soft-TKD refer to the Tikhonov-regularized initialization, not hard thresholding. The regularized null projection is a smooth spectral weighting, not a strict orthogonal null-space projection.

NeXtQSM is written as Next-QSM in the existing image headings. Both labels refer to the official published NeXtQSM model. Figure 3 uses the updated iQSM2 file whose SHA256 is recorded in the source provenance.
